mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes-Benz CLA 180d or 200d engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A replacement engine for a CLA 180d or 200d typically costs between £800 and £4,200 depending on the engine code and condition. Used OM607 units start from £800-£1,400, reconditioned from £1,500-£2,200, and fully rebuilt OM654 engines from £2,500-£4,200. Labour for supply & fit adds £450-£800.

mainEntity.name: Does the CLA 180d or 200d have a timing belt or timing chain?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the engine and generation. The OM607 (CLA 180d, 2013-2019) uses a timing belt that must be replaced every 80,000-100,000 miles. The OM651 (CLA 200d, 2013-2019) uses a timing chain at the rear of the engine that is prone to stretching. The OM654 (CLA 180d/200d, 2019-present) uses a timing chain that is generally more robust.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a CLA 200d?

acceptedAnswer.text: On OM651-equipped CLA 200d models (C117, 2013-2019), the most common symptom is a rattling or clattering noise from the rear of the engine on cold start. Other signs include loss of power, rough idle, engine misfires, and the engine management light illuminating. If you hear any unusual sounds, have the timing system inspected immediately - ignoring the rattle can lead to catastrophic engine failure.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Mercedes-Benz CLA 180d or 200d?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the generation and condition. A C117 CLA 180d or 200d is typically worth £4,000-£8,000 - a rebuilt engine (£1,800-£3,200) can be a worthwhile investment if the car is in good condition. A C118 CLA 180d or 200d is worth £10,000-£20,000 - a rebuilt OM654 engine (£2,500-£4,200) is usually well within the car's value. Always compare the cost of repair against the car's market value.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the CLA 180d and CLA 200d engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: In the C117 generation (2013-2019), the CLA 180d uses the Renault-sourced OM607 1.5-litre diesel (109 hp, 260 Nm) with a timing belt, while the CLA 200d uses Mercedes' own OM651 2.1-litre diesel (136 hp, 300 Nm) with a rear-mounted timing chain. In the C118 generation (2019-present), both badges use the OM654 2.0-litre diesel, with the 180d producing 116 hp and the 200d producing 150 hp.

mainEntity.name: What causes the Mercedes-Benz CLA 180d or 200d to lose power?

acceptedAnswer.text: Power loss in the CLA 180d and 200d depends on the engine and generation. On OM651 engines, timing chain stretch can cause cam timing drift, reducing power. On OM607 and OM651, EGR valve clogging, DPF blockage, or turbocharger actuator failure are common culprits. On OM654 engines, NOx sensor failure can trigger limp mode. A diagnostic check with Mercedes STAR or compatible equipment is essential to identify the exact cause.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes-Benz CLA 180d / 200d - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The CLA 180d and 200d badges represent the entry-level and mid-range diesel offerings across two generations of the Mercedes-Benz CLA. The first-generation C117 (2013-2019) used the Renault-sourced OM607 1.5-litre in the 180d and Mercedes' own OM651 2.1-litre in the 200d. The second-generation C118 (2019-present) consolidated both badges under the modular OM654 2.0-litre diesel, offering improved efficiency and reduced emissions.

milestones.description: OM607.951, 1.5L diesel, 109 hp (80 kW) - C117 CLA 180d launch; Renault K9K-sourced engine; timing belt instead of chain
OM651.930, 2.1L diesel, 136 hp (100 kW) - C117 CLA 200d launch; rear-mounted timing chain; 300 Nm torque
Facelift with revised engine management; power outputs unchanged; BlueEFFICIENCY tweaks introduced
OM654.920, 2.0L diesel, 150 hp (110 kW) - C118 CLA 200d launch; aluminium block with steel pistons; 320 Nm torque
OM654.920 (detuned), 2.0L diesel, 116 hp (85 kW) - C118 CLA 180d launch; 280 Nm torque
Model year updates with revised emissions calibration; OM654 continues

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes-Benz CLA 180d / 200d Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The CLA 180d and 200d have been powered by three distinct diesel engine families across the C117 and C118 generations - the Renault-sourced OM607 (180d), the Mercedes OM651 (200d), and the modular OM654 (both badges). Each has distinct failure patterns. Rebuilt CLA 180d and 200d engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components designed to address the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: OM651 Timing Chain Failure - Why the C117 CLA 200d Rattles on Cold Start
problems.rootCause: The OM651 uses a single timing chain located at the rear of the engine, adjacent to the gearbox. The chain stretches over time due to inadequate tensioner design and extended oil change intervals. A rattling or clattering noise on cold start for a few seconds is the classic warning sign.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, tensioner, guides, and sprockets (gearbox removal required)
repairOptions.longevity: Best done at first rattle; prevents catastrophic failure

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt OM651 with upgraded timing components
repairOptions.longevity: Required if chain has jumped; bent valves almost certain

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical C117 CLA 200d is worth £4,000-£8,000 depending on condition and mileage. For vehicles under £5,000, a preventative chain replacement (£1,400-£1,900) is usually the better financial decision than a full engine replacement. For higher-value examples, a rebuilt OM651 with warranty (£2,000-£3,200) offers peace of mind.
problems.recommendation: If you hear a rattling noise from the rear of the engine on cold starts - especially between 60,000 and 100,000 miles - act immediately. A preventative chain replacement at a specialist saves thousands compared to waiting for failure. Once the chain jumps, piston-to-valve contact is almost certain and engine replacement becomes the only viable option.

problems.group: OM607 Timing Belt & Injector Seal Failure
problems.h4: OM607 Timing Belt & Injector Seal Failure - The Renault-Sourced Engine's Weak Points
problems.rootCause: The OM607 is a Renault K9K-sourced engine that uses a timing belt rather than a chain. The belt must be replaced every 80,000-100,000 miles - failure is catastrophic. Injector seal leakage ("black death") is also common, causing diesel odour, misfiring, and potential injector seizure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing belt, tensioner, water pump
repairOptions.longevity: Essential maintenance; do not exceed 100k miles

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove injectors, replace seals and bolts
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if injectors are not seized

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt engine with new belt and injector seals
repairOptions.longevity: Required if belt has snapped or injectors are seized

problems.recommendation: Unlike the OM651's timing chain, the OM607's timing belt failure is predictable and preventable. If your OM607-equipped CLA 180d is approaching 80,000 miles or 5 years since the last belt change, replace it immediately. A £350-£650 specialist belt change is far cheaper than a £1,800+ engine replacement.
problems.cta: -> Compare OM607 timing belt replacement and engine prices for your CLA 180d

problems.group: OM654 Cold-Start Misfire & NOx Sensor Failure
problems.h4: OM654 Cold-Start Misfire & NOx Sensor Failure - C118 CLA 180d / 200d Quirks
problems.rootCause: The OM654 engine is known for a cold-start misfire and shaking that lasts for up to 30 seconds, with Mercedes dealers describing it as a "normal characteristic" of the engine. NOx sensor failures are also common, triggering the check engine light. Early production units may have crankshaft issues.

Diagnostic scan, software update, injector calibration
Complete engine with updated emissions components
repairOptions.longevity: Only if engine damage has occurred

problems.recommendation: If your C118 CLA 180d or 200d experiences cold-start misfiring, have the NOx sensors and injector calibration checked. While Mercedes may describe the shaking as "normal," persistent misfires should be investigated. A £600-£1,200 NOx sensor replacement is significantly cheaper than a full engine replacement.

problems.h4: OM651 & OM607 EGR Cooler & DPF Issues - Diesel Emission System Failures
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes-Benz CLA 180d and 200d (OM607.951 and OM651.930, C117, 2013-2019)
problems.rootCause: The EGR cooler can develop micro-cracks, causing coolant loss and potential engine overheating. DPF clogging is common on vehicles used predominantly for short urban journeys.

repairOptions.longevity: Required if coolant ingestion or DPF failure has caused engine damage
